heroHeadline: ASCO 2026 Opens: CROWN Trial Shows 60% of ALK+ NSCLC Patients Progression-Free at 5 Years; Decnupaz Approved for Rare Blood Cancer
heroSubtitle: The 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting opened May 29 in Chicago with landmark data across lung cancer, multiple myeloma, and breast cancer. The CROWN trial's 7-year lorlatinib update showed approximately 60% of ALK-positive NSCLC patients progression-free at 5 years with 92% CNS protection — among the most remarkable targeted therapy outcomes ever reported. The HARMONi-6 trial demonstrated ivonescimab, a first-in-class dual PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, achieves 11.1 vs. 6.9 months PFS versus anti-PD-1 alone in squamous NSCLC. Dana-Farber reported 100% MRD-negativity in high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma treated with CAR-T. The NEJM published ASCENT-03 on May 28, confirming sacituzumab govitecan's superiority over chemotherapy in PD-1-ineligible TNBC. The FDA approved Decnupaz (pivekimab sunirine) on May 27 for BPDCN, a rare and aggressive blood cancer. The marquee daraxonrasib pancreatic cancer Phase 3 plenary (RASolute 302) is scheduled for May 31.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA Drug Approvals, NIH/NCI, peer-reviewed journals (NEJM, The Lancet, Nature Medicine), ASCO/ESMO/AACR conference data, and institutional analyses. All clinical data reflect published and presented trial results.
